# package wire

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-s7comm/wire"
```

Package wire provides S7 PDU encoding and parsing (headers, read/write, setup, SZL, blocks) plus S7 TSAP helpers. Live transport uses go-cotp TSDUs; this package does not own TPKT or COTP framing.

Parsing philosophy: the wire layer is strict on framing and declared lengths—buffers are validated, lengths are checked, and overruns or mismatches return errors. Semantic interpretation (e.g. best-effort field extraction, device-dependent layouts) is left to the client and model layers.

```go
const (
	UserdataReq = 0x11 // method: request
	UserdataRes = 0x12 // method: response, and a client's follow-up request
	// UserdataSubParam is the type and function group byte of an SZL read
	// request: type 4 (request) and group 4 (CPU functions).
	UserdataSubParam = 0x44
	UserdataSZL      = 0x01 // subfunction: read SZL

	UserdataTypeRequest  = 0x40 // type nibble of a request (high bits of the type/group byte)
	UserdataTypeResponse = 0x80 // type nibble of a response
	UserdataGroupBlock   = 0x03 // function group: block functions
	UserdataGroupCPU     = 0x04 // function group: CPU functions (SZL)

	UserdataBlockCount = 0x01 // block functions: count blocks of each type
	UserdataBlockList  = 0x02 // block functions: list blocks of one type
	UserdataBlockInfo  = 0x03 // block functions: get block info
)
```

User data parameter fields. A request parameter is 00 01 12 04 | method 0x11 | type and function group | subfunction | sequence; a response or follow-up parameter is 00 01 12 08 | method 0x12 | type and group | subfunction | sequence | data unit reference | last data unit | error code (2 bytes). This is the layout Snap7, STEP 7 5.5, TIA Portal V13, WinCC Advanced and libnodave send and S7-300/S7-400 CPUs answer (testdata/captures).

### func BuildTSAP

```go
func BuildTSAP(connType, rack, slot int) (uint16, error)
```

BuildTSAP creates a TSAP from connection type, rack, and slot (S7 convention). Connection type: 1=PG, 2=OP, 3=S7Basic (0..255). Rack must be 0..7, slot 0..31; returns error if out of range.

### func EncodeRackSlotTSAP

### func EncodeS7Any

```go

```

EncodeS7Any encodes an S7Any address specification (syntax SyntaxIDS7Any only). Call ValidateArea(addr.Area) before encoding if area comes from untrusted input. ### func NormalizeResponseDataLength

```go
func NormalizeResponseDataLength(transportSize ResponseTransportSize, rawLength uint16) (payloadBytes int, err error)
```

NormalizeResponseDataLength converts the length field of a Read Var answer item to its payload byte count. The field counts bits for BYTE/WORD/DWORD (0x04) and INTEGER (0x05), and bytes for DINTEGER (0x06), REAL (0x07) and OCTET STRING (0x09), as Wireshark's s7comm dissector reads it. A BIT item (0x03) carries one bit in one byte; its length, normally 1, is rounded up to whole bytes. Any other transport size is an error.

### func ParamErrorCodeString

```go
func ParamErrorCodeString(code uint16) string
```

ParamErrorCodeString returns a human-readable string for the 16-bit S7 parameter error code. Codes are from the S7 parameter section of responses (block, upload, diagnostics, etc.). Unknown codes return a formatted hex string.

### func ParamErrorFromParam

```go
func ParamErrorFromParam(param []byte) (code uint16, ok bool)
```

ParamErrorFromParam reads the 16-bit parameter error code at the standard offset (bytes 2-3, big-endian). Many S7 Ack-Data parameter sections carry this code when the response indicates an error. Returns (code, true) if param has at least 4 bytes; otherwise (0, false).

#### func InspectTPDU

```go
func InspectTPDU(tpdu []byte) (*FrameSummary, error)
```

InspectTPDU decodes a COTP TPDU payload (no TPKT header) and extracts high-level S7 metadata when present. This is a diagnostic helper for offline captures; the live client path uses cotp.Conn TSDUs. For full TPKT captures, peel the TPKT header with go-tpkt first, then pass the TPDU payload here.

### type ROSCTR

ROSCTR is the S7 message type (Remote Operating Service Control).

```go
const (
```


ReadVarResult is one item of a Read Var answer. RawLength is the wire length field (bits or bytes, by transport size); a failed item has TransportSize 0x00, RawLength 0 and no Data.

### type ResponseTransportSize

```go
type ResponseTransportSize byte
```

ResponseTransportSize is the data transport size of a Read Var answer item (or a Write Var data item). It is not the request transport size of an S7ANY address: use the DataTransportSize\* constants for its values.

```go
const (
	RespTransportSizeBit       ResponseTransportSize = 0x01
	RespTransportSizeByte      ResponseTransportSize = 0x02
	RespTransportSizeChar      ResponseTransportSize = 0x03
	RespTransportSizeWord      ResponseTransportSize = 0x04
	RespTransportSizeInt       ResponseTransportSize = 0x05
	RespTransportSizeDWord     ResponseTransportSize = 0x06
	RespTransportSizeDInt      ResponseTransportSize = 0x07
	RespTransportSizeReal      ResponseTransportSize = 0x08
	RespTransportSizeDATE      ResponseTransportSize = 0x09
	RespTransportSizeTOD       ResponseTransportSize = 0x0A
	RespTransportSizeTIME      ResponseTransportSize = 0x0B
	RespTransportSizeS5TIME    ResponseTransportSize = 0x0C
	RespTransportSizeDT        ResponseTransportSize = 0x0F
	RespTransportSizeCount     ResponseTransportSize = 0x1C
	RespTransportSizeTimer     ResponseTransportSize = 0x1D
	RespTransportSizeIECCount  ResponseTransportSize = 30
	RespTransportSizeIECTimer  ResponseTransportSize = 31
	RespTransportSizeHSCounter ResponseTransportSize = 32
)
```

Deprecated: these constants copy request transport sizes (and S7-200 types) and are not data transport sizes; only 0x03 (BIT), 0x04, 0x05, 0x06, 0x07 and 0x09 occur in an answer. Use DataTransportSizeBit, DataTransportSizeByte, DataTransportSizeInt, DataTransportSizeDInt, DataTransportSizeReal and DataTransportSizeOctet. Kept so that existing code compiles; NormalizeResponseDataLength refuses the values that are not data transport sizes.

#### func (ResponseTransportSize) String

```go
func (r ResponseTransportSize) String() string
```

String returns the data transport size name as Wireshark's s7comm dissector gives it (e.g. "BYTE/WORD/DWORD", "REAL"); other values in hex.


S7Error represents an S7 protocol error

#### func NewS7Error

```go
func NewS7Error(class, code byte) *S7Error
```

NewS7Error creates a new S7 error preserving raw Class and Code, with a string mapping when known. Header-level errors use Class and Code; item-level return codes use Code only (Class zero).

#### func NewS7ErrorWithParam

```go
func NewS7ErrorWithParam(class, code byte, param []byte) *S7Error
```

NewS7ErrorWithParam is like NewS7Error but when param contains a 16-bit parameter error code at the standard offset (bytes 2-3), uses ParamErrorCodeString for the message when that code is non-zero. This yields clearer errors (e.g. "block not found", "invalid request length") for block/upload/diagnostic responses.

#### func (S7Error) Error

```go
func (e *S7Error) Error() string
```

```go
}
```

SZLResponse holds a parsed SZL response

#### func ParseSZLResponse

```go
func ParseSZLResponse(data []byte) (*SZLResponse, error)
```

ParseSZLResponse parses the first packet of a SZL read response from the S7 data payload. Strict: validates return code, data length, and minimum 8-byte header. When the CPU marks the response "more data follows" (ParseUserdataParam), the next packets carry only further records: append their ParseUserdataData payloads to Data.

### type UploadChunk

```go

	Done bool
	Data []byte
}
```

UploadChunk is one chunk returned by upload continuation responses.

#### func ParseUploadResponse

```go
func ParseUploadResponse(param, data []byte) (*UploadChunk, error)
```

ParseUploadResponse parses an upload response. The parameter's status byte is 0x01 while more data follows, 0x00 for the last segment. The data section is the segment length in bytes (2 bytes), 2 further bytes, then the segment. Strict: the length must not overrun the data section.

```go
}
```

### type VarSpec

```go
type VarSpec struct {
	Syntax        byte
	TransportSize byte   // request transport size (TransportSize* constants)
	Count         uint16 // element count
	DBNumber      uint16
	Area          byte
	StartBit      uint32 // 24-bit address in bits; for timers and counters the element number
}
```

VarSpec is one item of a Read Var or Write Var job. The raw fields are as on the wire. An S7ANY item (SyntaxIDS7Any) fills the address fields; the ranges of a DBREAD item (SyntaxIDDBRead) come from ParseReadVarDBRead; any other syntax leaves the address fields zero.
